stem:
Riya draws this feeding diagram for a school garden in her science notebook. In it, grass is eaten by both a grasshopper and a rabbit; the grasshopper is eaten by a frog and a sparrow; the frog is eaten by a snake; the rabbit is eaten by a fox; and the sparrow and the snake are both eaten by an eagle.

What should Riya call this diagram?

options.text: A food chain, because it starts with grass, which is a producer
A food web, because the organisms are connected through many interlinked feeding paths
A food chain, because the arrows show the flow of energy in one direction
A food web, because it contains more than three organisms

teacher.key_rationale: The diagram shows grass eaten by two consumers and the grasshopper eaten by two consumers, so feeding paths branch and interlink; by the taught rule, many interlinked feeding paths make a food web, not a single linear food chain. Distractor A wrongly uses 'starts with a producer', C wrongly uses 'arrows show one-way energy flow' (true of webs too), and D wrongly uses a mere organism count instead of the interlinking test. Key B.
teacher.figure_note: Diagram added per spec: directed feeding graph (grass -> grasshopper/rabbit; grasshopper -> frog/sparrow; frog -> snake; rabbit -> fox; snake and sparrow -> eagle). Stem refers to this figure.
